text: Where should an exception be caught?
choices: Only at the top of `main`, so all error handling is in one place.
As close to the throw as possible, so the failure does not propagate through unrelated code.
Where something meaningful can be done: retry, fall back, report to a user, record and continue, or add context and rethrow.
In every method that calls something which might fail, so no failure goes unnoticed.
explanation: If none of those applies at this point, do not catch. Catching feels responsible and letting an exception through feels careless, but it is the other way round: a catch that does not improve the situation has only hidden information. Most programs want handling concentrated at a few boundaries — the top of a request, a task, a user action, or `main`.
